extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism/adjudication layer. Claims are limited to evidence supported by this paper; prior membrane-disruption statements are retained as context rather than upgraded to direct mechanism evidence for every assay in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports anticancer cytotoxicity of the 9-mer peptides through short-exposure MTT viability assays across carcinoma, neuroblastoma, lymphoma, CHO, normal-cell, and RBC contexts.
mechanism_claims.limitations: MTT/hemolysis assays support cytotoxic phenotype and selectivity, not a molecular target mechanism by themselves.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The CHO-K1 versus pgsA-745 comparison supports a cell-surface GAG effect on cytotoxic susceptibility for LTX-302 and LTX-318, while LTX-315 is reported as not discriminating between those two CHO contexts.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay distinguishes GAG-present versus GAG-deficient cell contexts; it does not identify a single molecular receptor.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports stronger peptide interaction with heparan sulfate than chondroitin sulfate using soluble GAG inhibition and CS/HS-Sepharose affinity measurements.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=22:Effect of soluble GAGs on cytotoxic activity;xml:table=5;xml:fig=5

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports GAG interaction/modulation, not antimicrobial killing mechanism or a standalone AMP potency endpoint.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The article background discusses prior evidence that LTX-302 disrupts tumor plasma membrane and that CAPs can increase membrane permeability; worker-6 retains this only as cited contextual mechanism evidence.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The current paper did not directly re-measure membrane disruption as a primary mechanism endpoint for all three peptides.
